A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RuleReasoner/DADS research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, with retained material identifiable despite reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation of 4B/8B models, including eight in-distribution tasks, three out-of-distribution benchmarks, sampling analyses, and appendix robustness and test-time-scaling results.

after.justification: V2 reports original model evaluations, curriculum comparisons, hyperparameter sensitivity experiments, additional reasoning benchmarks, and training-data ablations in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the specified unnormalized sampling weight from exp((v+epsilon)/tau) to exp(v/tau)+epsilon, affecting normalized sampling probabilities. The reward function, GRPO objective, and historical-reward reweighting framework remain. Newly documented entropy removal and rule shuffling do not establish when those implementation choices were introduced.

E1.justification: V2 adds inference-only evaluations on AIME 2025, GPQA Diamond, and Coin Flip, extending coverage to mathematical, scientific, and symbolic reasoning. Appendix C.9 additionally uses AIME 1983–2024 for training experiments. The original eight-task collection is retained under the name RULECOLLECTION-32K with unchanged reported dataset counts.

E2.justification: V2 Table 2 adds Data-balance RL, Easy-to-hard RL, and ADARFT to the existing ID comparison. Appendix comparisons additionally evaluate Easy-to-hard SFT and DAPO with dynamic sampling; v1 explicitly disabled DAPO's dynamic sampling. These substantially expand the evaluated alternatives to the proposed sampling strategy.

E3.justification: New protocols include eight difficulty partitions for progressive curricula, balanced resampling to 3,571 examples per domain, individual hyperparameter sweeps, and AR-LSAT evaluations every 50 steps in a dedicated ablation. V2 also introduces math-only, rule-only, and joint-data GRPO controls without DADS. The original main training and inference settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds sensitivity tests for alpha, tau, and epsilon; a DADS-versus-no-DADS learning comparison on difficult AR-LSAT examples; and training-data composition ablations. Table 15 adds before/after reasoning cases supporting the new mechanism discussion. V1's rule-noise, difficulty-level, and test-time-scaling analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: V2 removes v1's statement that one-sided p-values are reported, while retaining five evaluation runs, mean/standard-deviation reporting, and seeds {21,42,84}. Figures 5–7 acquire shaded bands, but their statistical meaning is unspecified. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new results appear: Table 6 reports OOD averages of 81.7 for DADS, 78.1 for ADARFT, and 75.4 for dynamic-sampling DAPO; Table 8 adds DADS scores of 23.3, 44.9, and 95.1 on AIME 2025, GPQA Diamond, and Coin Flip. Original headline results remain. Figure 7 changes the GRPO/DAPO curve assignments and revises the reported efficiency comparison from approximately 100 fewer steps versus GRPO to 72 versus DAPO.

T1.justification: The revised weighting definition in Algorithm 1 is mathematically substantive: epsilon cancels during normalization in v1, whereas v2's additive epsilon affects the resulting distribution. The GRPO equations remain unchanged, and neither version provides a theorem or proof establishing DADS guarantees.

C1.justification: V2's introduction presents RULECOLLECTION-32K as a released dataset contribution and emphasizes training regularization for stable reasoning in small models. V1 instead emphasizes data curation and outcome-based verification. The central claims about generalizable rule reasoning, adaptive domain sampling, and improved efficiency remain, including the headline performance margins.

C2.justification: New Section 5.5 attributes generalization partly to meta-introspection, self-verification, and consistency checking. Appendix C adds interpretations concerning difficult-domain allocation, hyperparameter behavior, and the necessity of rule-centric training data. V2 also removes the explicit statement that extrapolation to long compositional reasoning chains remains unverified, while retaining noise, model-scaling, and possible BBH-contamination caveats.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly documents entropy-bonus removal and training-rule shuffling, and Appendix C.8 supplies curriculum implementation recipes. The hardware and main hyperparameter table remain. However, direct code/model links are replaced by a future-release statement, and the new o3-mini attribution for long-CoT distillation conflicts with the retained DeepSeek-R1 description in Appendix B.2.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused positioning against loss-based and proxy-model data-mixture approaches, citing Velocitune, DIDS, and RegMix, alongside new curriculum-learning references. It also adds long-context motivation. The broader relationship to rule-based reasoning and RLVR literature remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and data-curation prose are edited and condensed, and terminology is standardized around RULECOLLECTION-32K. Analyses become a standalone Section 5, ethics moves out of the appendix, and a reproducibility statement is added. Much of the existing technical prose and overall argument sequence is retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a substantially different conference layout, expands the ID table with a curriculum block, and adds multiple comparison, ablation, and trajectory tables. The dataset-statistics table moves to the appendix and loses its Source column. Figures 5–7 gain shaded bands and a speedup annotation; Figure 10 uses tighter axes and adds pass@1 reference lines.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central sampling contribution. V1 disabled DAPO's dynamic sampling and lacked direct curriculum comparisons; v2 evaluates these alternatives and adds DADS/no-DADS, hyperparameter, and training-data controls. These address important gaps in attribution and robustness despite unchanged headline scores. The gains outweigh weaker resource-access guidance and conflicting SFT-teacher documentation, although the new meta-introspection explanation remains supported mainly by illustrative cases.
